rows.jyutping: gwai3 dou3 ling6 jan4 koek3 bou6
rows.note: Use this when the price is so high that it puts someone off or beyond their budget.

example.english: The prices at this restaurant are prohibitive—one meal costs over a thousand dollars.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳啲菜貴到令人卻步，食一餐要成千蚊。
example.jyutping: ne1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 coi3 gwai3 dou3 ling6 jan4 koek3 bou6 sik6 jat1 caan1 jiu3 sing4 cin1 man1

rows.jyutping: naan4 dou3 ling6 jan4 koek3 bou6
rows.note: Use this when something requires so much effort or skill that it deters people.

example.english: The difficulty of this assignment is prohibitive; I want to give up before starting.
example.traditional: 呢份功課難到令人卻步，未開始做我已經想放棄。
example.jyutping: ne1 fan6 gung1 fo3 naan4 dou3 ling6 jan4 koek3 bou6 mei6 hoi1 ci2 zou6 ngo5 ji5 ging1 soeng2 fong3 hei3

rows.note: Use this for authorities, rules, or institutions that are very restrictive; it is the everyday choice for the ‘tending to forbid’ sense.

example.english: The estate has prohibitive rules; even keeping a dog requires an application.
example.traditional: 呢間屋苑管得好嚴，養狗都要先申請。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 uk1 jyun2 gun2 dak1 hou2 jim4 joeng5 gau2 dou1 jiu3 sin1 san1 cing2
